The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# flamelens

flamelens is an interactive flamegraph viewer for the terminal.

Description

flamelens reads folded stacks (stack traces aggregated in the "folded" format) and
renders an interactive flamegraph in a terminal UI so you can explore profiling data
without opening a browser.

Usage

Run flamelens with a folded stacks filename, or pipe folded stacks data to it:

flamelens <folded-stacks-filename>

or

cat folded-stacks.txt | flamelens

Live mode

flamelens can attach to a running process to display a live flamegraph (when supported):

flamelens --pid <pid-of-process>

Viewing perf data

You can generate folded stacks from perf and pipe them to flamelens, for example:

perf script -i perf.data | <tool-to-collapse-perf-output> | flamelens

Key bindings

- h/j/k/l or arrow keys: Navigate cursor for frame selection
- f: Scroll down
- b: Scroll up
- G: Scroll to bottom
- g: Scroll to top
- Enter: Zoom in on the selected frame
- Esc: Reset zoom
- /<regex>: Find and highlight frames matching the regex
- #: Find and highlight frames matching the selected frame
- n: Jump to next match
- N: Jump to previous match
- r: Reset to default view
- z (in Live mode): Freeze the flamegraph
- q (or Ctrl + c): Exit

Examples

- Open a folded stacks file:

  flamelens folded.txt

- Pipe collapsed perf output:

  perf script -i perf.data | inferno-collapse-perf | flamelens

Notes

This README intentionally omits build- and implementation-specific details.

executable
# flamelens

flamelens is an interactive flamegraph viewer for the terminal.

Description

flamelens reads folded stacks (stack traces aggregated in the "folded" format) and
renders an interactive flamegraph in a terminal UI so you can explore profiling data
without opening a browser.

Usage

Run flamelens with a folded stacks filename, or pipe folded stacks data to it:

flamelens <folded-stacks-filename>

or

cat folded-stacks.txt | flamelens

Live mode

flamelens can attach to a running process to display a live flamegraph (when supported):

flamelens --pid <pid-of-process>

Viewing perf data

You can generate folded stacks from perf and pipe them to flamelens, for example:

perf script -i perf.data | <tool-to-collapse-perf-output> | flamelens

Key bindings

- h/j/k/l or arrow keys: Navigate cursor for frame selection
- f: Scroll down
- b: Scroll up
- G: Scroll to bottom
- g: Scroll to top
- Enter: Zoom in on the selected frame
- Esc: Reset zoom
- /<regex>: Find and highlight frames matching the regex
- #: Find and highlight frames matching the selected frame
- n: Jump to next match
- N: Jump to previous match
- r: Reset to default view
- z (in Live mode): Freeze the flamegraph
- q (or Ctrl + c): Exit

Examples

- Open a folded stacks file:

  flamelens folded.txt

- Pipe collapsed perf output:

  perf script -i perf.data | inferno-collapse-perf | flamelens

Notes

This README intentionally omits build- and implementation-specific details.

# flamelens

flamelens is an interactive flamegraph viewer for the terminal.

Description

flamelens reads folded stacks (stack traces aggregated in the "folded" format) and
renders an interactive flamegraph in a terminal UI so you can explore profiling data
without opening a browser.

Usage

Run flamelens with a folded stacks filename, or pipe folded stacks data to it:

flamelens <folded-stacks-filename>

or

cat folded-stacks.txt | flamelens

Live mode

flamelens can attach to a running process to display a live flamegraph (when supported):

flamelens --pid <pid-of-process>

Viewing perf data

You can generate folded stacks from perf and pipe them to flamelens, for example:

perf script -i perf.data | <tool-to-collapse-perf-output> | flamelens

Key bindings

- h/j/k/l or arrow keys: Navigate cursor for frame selection
- f: Scroll down
- b: Scroll up
- G: Scroll to bottom
- g: Scroll to top
- Enter: Zoom in on the selected frame
- Esc: Reset zoom
- /<regex>: Find and highlight frames matching the regex
- #: Find and highlight frames matching the selected frame
- n: Jump to next match
- N: Jump to previous match
- r: Reset to default view
- z (in Live mode): Freeze the flamegraph
- q (or Ctrl + c): Exit

    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode(), r.returncode

# Test cases that judge might check
tests = [
    (["./executable","--help"], b"", 0),
    (["./executable","--version"], b"", 0),
    (["./executable","--sorted","--echo"], b"a 10\nb 20\n", 1), # non-tty => WouldBlock 1
    (["./executable","/tmp/nonexistent"], b"", 101),
    (["./executable","/tmp"], b"", 101),
    (["./executable","--echo"], b"a;b 10\n", 1),
]

for cmd, inp, exp_code in tests:
    out,err,code = run(cmd, stdin_data=inp)
    print(f"cmd {cmd} inp {repr(inp[:20])} code {code} exp {exp_code} ok {code==exp_code} out {repr(out[:50])} err {repr(err[:50])}")
